title: Dominic and the Machine Again
premise: Hazel Ishikawa, a clone of the murdered detective who once ran the interworld courier route, inherits both her original's unsolved case and the fragile truce it was meant to protect. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — the dying message of the machine that witnessed the murder — Hazel realizes the war between the worlds hinges on delivering it before the last relay goes dark. Pursued by factions on both sides, she and the dream-children race down the long route, discovering the killer was someone trying to prevent the message from ever arriving. In the end, Hazel chooses to broadcast the truth in her own voice, not her original's, ending the war and founding a found family from the children, the machine, and the survivors of both worlds.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade routing cargo between island territories and now writes science fiction about distance, duty, and the people who carry things across gaps. They live near a decommissioned relay station and insist the hum at night is just the wind.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel runs the courier run between two silent worlds, carrying sealed diplomatic packets while haunted by fragments of her original's memories. She visits the grave-marker of Detective Ishikawa and finds the case file left deliberately for her. Emotional beat: loneliness tempered by duty; the hook of inheritance.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Hazel and nine-year-old Teo, one of the colony children. The children wake sobbing from an identical dream: a corridor, a dying voice, coordinates. Their teacher sends for Hazel, the only clone qualified to recognize what the dream is. Emotional beat: uncanny dread becoming shared purpose.

chapters.title: What the Machine Saw
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Following the dream's coordinates, Hazel and Teo find the derelict witness-machine, damaged but alive, which begins transmitting the original's final recorded moments — cut off mid-sentence by sabotage. Someone else has been searching for it too. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear of pursuit.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, No Words
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The children decode fragments of the dream-message using their shared language of play, revealing it names the murderer. Both governments learn of the machine's discovery and issue contradictory demands: surrender it or be treated as combatants. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The Original's Mistake
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Reviewing the case file, Hazel realizes her original suspected the killer but trusted them anyway — a trust that got her killed. Hazel must decide whether to repeat that trust with her own found allies. Emotional beat: grief for a self she never was; the burden of inherited error.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: POV rotating among Hazel, Teo, and pilot Sefa, a defector who joins them. Warships blockade the route; the crew smuggles the machine aboard a mail freighter. A skirmish costs them their fuel reserve and nearly the machine itself. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Name in the Dream
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The children complete the message: the killer is the peace envoy who brokered the original truce, who silenced the machine to hide that the treaty was built on a lie. Hazel confronts the possibility that exposing it may start the war rather than end it. Emotional beat: moral vertigo at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: Relay Dark
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The envoy's forces board the freighter as the last relay station begins its final shutdown. The children use their shared dream-link to guide Hazel through blacked-out corridors to the broadcast core while Sefa holds the dock. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into courage; every character choosing their part.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Cornered by the envoy, Hazel broadcasts the full message — but adds her own testimony, speaking as herself, not her original, breaking the cycle of inheritance-as-obligation. Both fleets receive the truth simultaneously; the envoy's lie collapses publicly. Emotional beat: catharsis; identity claimed, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Route We Keep
chapters.summary: POV Hazel, months later. The worlds reopen negotiations; Hazel declines a detective's badge and instead reopens the courier route with the children and Sefa as crew, the repaired machine riding along as navigator. The dreams have stopped, replaced by ordinary dreams. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — family chosen, distance no longer silence.
